Members Open Meeting: Thursday 8th October St Ives Corn Exchange 1.20 for 2.00pm THE LIFE, MUSIC AND INFLUENCE OF BUDDY HOLLY Speaker: Tony Tutton Articles and features for the November newsletter should be sent to Anne by 17th October: editor@u3aivo.uk Newsletter October 2026 Website: u3aivo.uk, email: info@u3aivo.uk Or call 07458 197372 All Members Open Meetings are held at the Corn Exchange, St Ives 1.20pm for 2.00pm start. Please note: We kindly ask that members wishing to discuss membership matters or to book outings or theatre trips please arrive early to avoid disruption. Committee members and the Group Support Team will be available after the meeting to answer questions and discuss any matters of concern. Tony will take you on a journey through the life of the legendary Buddy Holly from his birthplace in Lubbock Texas in 1936 to his untimely death on 3rd February 1959. The talk features many of Buddy smash hits, That’ll be the Day, Oh Boy, Peggy Sue, Rave On, Heartbeat …and lots more.

3 Review of the Choir of Man Booking Procedure for Outings, Theatre Trips and Events PLEASE DO NOT PAY FOR TRIPS BEFORE YOUR BOOKING HAS BEEN CONFIRMED • Bookings can be made at Open Meetings or on the website • Theatre Trips: u3aivo.uk/theatre • Outings: u3aivo.uk/outings • Events: u3aivo.uk/events • Outings: Sue Belcher (07778425052 — Strictly for members with no internet) • When booking a trip on the web page, click on the blue envelope, please DO NOT click on 'CONTACT' at the very top of the page. • ALWAYS BOOK BEFORE PAYING. All bookings will be confirmed. • BACS payment preferred please, either online or by going into your branch • Payment: St Ives (Cambs) U3A Social Account • Sort code: 40 - 16 - 08 Account: 74557352 • Ref: u3a membership number and trip name • If no alternative, cheques made payable to: St Ives (Cambs) U3A Social Account • Payment to be made at least six weeks prior to the trip Or should that be the “Choir of Men”. Nine exceptional talented, versatile performers with an incredible vocal range from baritone to soprano entertain an audience in a high energy alternative musical. Encompassing everything from folk, to rock to heavy metal. Set in a community working-man’s pub bar, the story line is loosely based on a place where people come and share their troubles. It doesn’t matter who you are or where you come from. There’s humour, tap dancing on bar and table top, audience participation is encouraged, joining the cast on stage at the start of each act. You only know the performance is starting when they leave and the house lights dim. All were multi- talented singing, dancing, playing a variety of instruments as solos or combined, their timing couldn’t be faulted. This was complemented by excellent sound and lighting of the set on stage. If I have one criticism it is not of the show, but the seating. These were probably the most uncomfortable seats I have sat on in a theatre—a bench seat would have been better! Hopefully these will get replaced along with the rest of the renovations that are going on at the moment at the Cliffs Pavilion, Southend. Graham Emmett
‘ u3a ’ s Got Talent ’ Friday 16 th October AN EVENING OF ENTERTAINMENT BY OUR CREATIVE ARTS GROUPS (but no judging involved!) ST IVES CORN EXCHANGE, DOORS OPEN 6.30PM TICKETS £5 (or £3 for performers) The Corn Exchange has limited capacity so please book tickets as soon as possible. Our music groups have sometimes provided background music at group fairs, but this event is being organised in response to a request from members who said they would welcome the opportunity to sit and listen to more of their performances, without the hubbub of a group fair. Seating will be round tables with the bar open to purchase drinks, and art & craft work will be on display to view before the event and during the interval. The evening will comprise a varied programme with performances by our music and singing groups, interspersed with stories and poetry. The evening is being organised by the Events Team and needs to be self - financing, in the same way as our quiz nights and other events are, which means the cost of hiring the hall and bar needs to be covered by ticket sales. To ease administration, groups taking part have been asked to block - book tickets for their members, but other members can book via the website in the usual way. The event web page will be updated regularly, so please check there for availability nearer the date, and come along to enjoy an evening of entertainment with your u3a friends. More details on the website here: u3a ’ s Got Talent

Vic Lelliot The Joy of Travelling After much deliberation it is with sadness that Julia Bowman has decided to close this group. It has been running for over two years but with dwindling numbers (mainly because everyone is travelling all the time!) it’s now going to end. If anyone wants to start a similar group then please get in touch with the Group Support Team. gst@u3aivo.uk Sailing Group …. underway and making way Following an initial article in the June magazine 10 members of St Ives u3a came forward and expressed an interest in yacht sailing. During three days in late August nine members of the group each enjoyed a day on the water. We sailed on the estuaries of the Rivers Orwell and Stour, and a little out to sea beyond Harwich and Felixstowe. Each day was rounded off with dinner in The Ship at Levington prior to the drive home. Fortunately, the good weather held (a little damp when we arrived at the boat on the third day, but sunny by afternoon) and everyone was able to experience some good sailing. On the last day we even saw the research vessel Sir David Attenborough coming back into Harwich from its recent trip to the arctic. Sailing Group Roger Beaman
Kayaking and Canoeing Group I ﬁrst paddled a kayak on a Scout camp at Bala in 1972. It’s fair to say that I have been paddling canoes and kayaks ever since, with a trip down the Grand Canyon, a week of paddling around the Isles of Scilly, a circumnavigation of Menorca and six days of Norwegian fjords and coastline being some of the highlights of the past 11 years. While I am not suggesting doing any of those trips as part of u3a, I am suggesting a St Ives u3a canoeing and kayaking group for those able to paddle and with their own equipment. If you are interested in joining like-minded people bobbing about on local (and maybe not so local) waters, then I’d like to hear from you. I have both an open canoe and several kayaks (including sea and whitewater, and even a 3-man kayak if you want to bring your partner and the dog), so happy to use a single or a double blade when on the water. This is not an invitation to have paddling lessons from me (I can point you in the direction of 3 clubs in the county that can help), although if you want a few tips and tricks, I am happy to help. And while I do have what I consider to be a reasonable amount of paddling gear, I am not a general outﬁtter for u3a. Initially I envisage some simple trips on the local rivers, but very happy to discuss looking further aﬁeld if people want to travel. Interested? Group Support Team 9 The Group Support Team comprises of Anne Bannell, Joy Cooper and Alan Rogers at the moment. And although the amount of work generated by this group is not enormous, we all have other roles within the u3a and consequently, especially when one of us is away, we ﬁnd ourselves a little stretched. We would really love someone else to join us. If you can answer ‘Yes’ to any of these questions—do get in touch: • Are you already familiar with how groups work? • Do you get on well with all sorts of people? • Can you facilitate? ie. Set up a meeting with others who want to start a new group? • Spare a couple of hours a month to attend the GST monthly meeting? gst@u3aivo.uk Every Month at the Corn Exchange Anyone for Bridge? Following an exploratory meeting of members interested in a Bridge group, we have two people willing to teach beginners or “rusty” players, and some who would like to play social or “kitchen” Bridge, not too competitively but aiming to improve their game. We’re still gathering interest, probably aiming to start the group in the new year. Please let us know if you might be interested, and keep an eye on the website for any developments. u3aivo.uk/possible - bridge

12 Constable Country On a very hot day in August, I decided to put on my walking boots on and head to Constable Country in Suffolk. The area of big skies, quite lanes, fabulous walking. It's the area made famous by the painter John Constable 1776 - 1837. My walk started from Flatford Mill - this was built around 1733. The building is a 3 storey water mill that was used for grinding corn. John Constable's father brought Flatford Mill in 1784. In 1943 the National Trust purchased the Mill and Flatford House. After looking around Flatford Mill and Willy Lotts Cottage (The Hay Wain) we walked across the meadows following the River Stour to the pretty village of Dedham. Passing cows roaming the meadows and cooling off in the River Stour. In total the walk is 3 miles. Alternatively, you can take the river boat or even try out a paddle board up to Dedham. This year 2026 marks 250 years of John Constable - a year of exhibitions. Please do visit this area and enjoy tea and cake in the various tearooms. Stella Joyner
